summary.text: An amoeba is a cell or single-celled organism that can change its shape, mainly by extending and retracting pseudopods.
Amoebae do not form a single taxonomic group; they are found in every major lineage of eukaryotic organisms.
They move and feed with pseudopods, which are bulges of cytoplasm, and typically take in food by extending them to encircle and engulf it.

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: From 2.3 micrometres to deep-sea shells of 20 cm

facts.label: Feeding spot
facts.value: No mouth, and no fixed place for engulfing food

facts.label: Water control
facts.value: Most freshwater amoebae expel excess water with a contractile vacuole

items.prompt: A pond amoeba pumps out water with a contractile vacuole, but an ocean amoeba usually has none. Why?

options.label: Ocean amoebae are too small to ever need one
Pond amoebae have thicker walls to protect them
Pond water has fewer solutes than the cell, so water flows in
Ocean amoebae pump water out through pseudopods

items.explain: Freshwater is hypotonic to the cell, so water enters by osmosis and must be expelled. Marine amoebae are in balance with the surrounding water.

items.prompt: Under a microscope an amoeboid shows slender, thread-like pseudopods. Which group does that suggest?

options.label: Cercozoans, such as Euglypha and Gromia
Amoebozoans, such as those in the genus Amoeba
Foraminifera, which merge their pseudopods into nets
Radiolaria, with stiff needle-like projections

items.explain: Cercozoan amoeboids have slender, thread-like (filose) pseudopods; amoebozoans have bulbous ones, foraminifera net-like ones and radiolaria needle-like axopodia.

items.prompt: An amoeba meets a bacterium. With no mouth, how does it take the bacterium in?

options.label: It extends pseudopods around it and engulfs it
It swallows it through a permanent mouth at its front
It absorbs it through its cell wall
It kills it with a toxin first

items.explain: Amoebae typically ingest food by phagocytosis, extending pseudopods to encircle and engulf it. They have no mouth or cytostome.

items.prompt: Why do biologists no longer file all amoeboid organisms together in the old group Sarcodina?

options.label: None of its members turned out to have pseudopods
Its members all turned out to be animals
Its members turned out to have cell walls
Its members were shown not to share common descent

items.explain: Molecular phylogenetic studies have shown that Sarcodina is not a monophyletic group, so amoeboid organisms are no longer classified together.

items.prompt: You scoop pond water into a jar. What is most likely true of the amoebae in it?

options.label: All can easily be seen without a microscope
Most are microscopic, though a few giants can be seen with the naked eye
None are large enough to see, even the biggest
They are all about the size of bacteria

items.explain: Most free-living freshwater amoebae are microscopic, but some species, such as Pelomyxa palustris and Chaos carolinense, are large enough to see with the naked eye.

items.prompt: A colony of social amoebae, Dictyostelium discoideum, runs short of food. What may it do?

options.label: Mate and reproduce sexually, including meiosis
Stop moving until food returns
Grow a shell of sand grains
Divide faster to cover more ground

items.explain: Dictyostelium discoideum can undergo mating and sexual reproduction including meiosis when food is scarce.
